title: Isaiah’s vision concerning Judah
summary: Isaiah’s word concerns Judah and Jerusalem.

explicit_facts.text: Isaiah, son of Amoz, saw a word concerning Judah and Jerusalem.

unspecified_visual_details: What the vision looks like; whether Isaiah is shown; the setting.

narration.text: The word that Isaiah, the son of Amoz, saw concerning Judah and Jerusalem:

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The verse introduces a prophetic vision, not a narrated event in Judah or Jerusalem.
prohibited_inventions: Depicting Isaiah or events in Judah and Jerusalem as physically present without textual description.

title: Nations flow to the Lord’s house
summary: In the last days, the Lord’s house is established above the hills, and nations flow to it. People invite one another to go there to learn the Lord’s ways.

explicit_facts.text: In the last days, the mountain of the Lord’s house is established in the top of the mountains and exalted above the hills; all nations flow unto it.
Many people say to come to the mountain of the Lord and the house of the God of Jacob to be taught his ways and walk in his paths.
The law goes forth from Zion and the word of the Lord from Jerusalem.

reasonable_visual_inferences: People traveling toward a high mountain and gathering there.
unspecified_visual_details: The mountain’s appearance, architecture, era, and the identities and appearance of the people.

spoken_dialogue.text: Come ye, and let us go up to the mountain of the Lord, to the house of the God of Jacob;
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Many people

prohibited_inventions: Depicting God or Jacob as physically present; inventing a named temple or particular people.

title: Weapons become tools
summary: The Lord judges among nations and rebukes many people. Weapons are turned into farming tools, and nations no longer make war.

explicit_facts.text: The Lord judges among nations and rebukes many people.
People beat swords into plow-shares and spears into pruning-hooks; nation does not lift sword against nation or learn war.

reasonable_visual_inferences: People reshaping swords and spears into agricultural implements.
unspecified_visual_details: The people, location, tools’ design, and manner of judgment or rebuke.
doctrinal_or_story_notes: The cessation of war is a prophetic teaching about a future state.
prohibited_inventions: Showing a battle or inventing a visible divine judge.

title: Call to walk in the Lord’s light
summary: The house of Jacob is urged to walk in the Lord’s light and is said to have gone astray.

explicit_facts.text: The house of Jacob is called to walk in the light of the Lord and told that all have gone astray, each to wicked ways.

unspecified_visual_details: The speaker, hearers’ appearance, and setting.

spoken_dialogue.text: O house of Jacob, come ye and let us walk in the light of the Lord;
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Unspecified speaker

doctrinal_or_story_notes: This is an exhortation, not a narrated gathering.
prohibited_inventions: Showing the house of Jacob as a specific group or inventing a speaker.

title: The house of Jacob’s practices
summary: The passage describes the house of Jacob as replenished from the east, heeding soothsayers, and pleasing themselves with strangers’ children. The land has abundant wealth, horses, chariots, and idols made and worshiped by its people.

explicit_facts.text: The Lord has forsaken the house of Jacob because they are replenished from the east, hearken to soothsayers like the Philistines, and please themselves in the children of strangers.
Their land is full of silver, gold, treasures, horses, and chariots.
Their land is full of idols; they worship the work of their hands, which their fingers have made.

reasonable_visual_inferences: A landscape containing wealth, horses, chariots, and handmade idols.
unspecified_visual_details: Specific people, objects, buildings, and how the listed practices appear.
doctrinal_or_story_notes: These verses report conditions and practices; they do not narrate their enactment.
prohibited_inventions: Depicting soothsaying, encounters with strangers’ children, or idol-making as a specific event.

title: The unhumble are condemned
summary: Neither the mean man nor the great man humbles himself; the verse says not to forgive him.

explicit_facts.text: The mean man does not bow down, and the great man does not humble himself; the verse says not to forgive him.

unspecified_visual_details: The people and setting; whether “boweth not down” is literal or figurative.
doctrinal_or_story_notes: The verse expresses condemnation, not a distinct narrated action.
prohibited_inventions: Inventing a specific person or depicting a divine act of punishment.

title: Warning to the wicked
summary: The wicked are told to hide in rock and dust. The lofty and proud will be humbled, and the Lord alone exalted in the day of the Lord of Hosts.

explicit_facts.text: The wicked are told to enter the rock and hide in the dust because the fear of the Lord and the glory of his majesty will smite them.
The lofty looks of man and the haughtiness of men will be humbled, and the Lord alone exalted in that day.
The day of the Lord of Hosts comes upon all nations and the proud and lofty will be brought low.

unspecified_visual_details: Whether the warning is spoken aloud, the identity of its speaker, and any visible manifestation of the Lord.

spoken_dialogue.text: O ye wicked ones, enter into the rock, and hide thee in the dust,
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Unspecified speaker

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The humbling and exaltation language is prophetic teaching; no visible divine appearance is described.
prohibited_inventions: Depicting the Lord or his majesty as a visible figure; presenting the prophecy as a specific present-tense event.

title: The day of the Lord upon the lofty
summary: The prophecy names the cedars of Lebanon, oaks of Bashan, high mountains and hills, lifted-up nations and peoples, high towers and fenced walls, ships of the sea and Tarshish, and pleasant pictures as subject to the day of the Lord.

explicit_facts.text: The day of the Lord comes upon the cedars of Lebanon and oaks of Bashan.
It comes upon high mountains and hills, lifted-up nations, and every people.
It comes upon every high tower and fenced wall.
It comes upon ships of the sea, ships of Tarshish, and pleasant pictures.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The listed natural features and structures may be represented as objects named in the prophecy.
unspecified_visual_details: The meaning of “pleasant pictures,” the precise ships and structures, and any people or event.
doctrinal_or_story_notes: This is a catalogue in prophetic teaching, not a sequence of separate events.
prohibited_inventions: Showing destruction or depicting the day of the Lord as a particular visible event.

title: The Lord alone exalted
summary: Human loftiness and haughtiness are made low, the Lord alone is exalted, and idols are utterly abolished.

explicit_facts.text: The loftiness and haughtiness of man are made low, and the Lord alone is exalted in that day.
The idols are utterly abolished.

unspecified_visual_details: How the figurative humbling and abolishing are visually represented; whether the Lord appears.
doctrinal_or_story_notes: The Lord’s exaltation and human humbling are prophetic language; no visible divine appearance is described.
prohibited_inventions: Depicting the Lord or idol-abolition as a specific physical event.

title: People hide among rocks
summary: People go into rock holes and earth caves. A man casts away his silver and gold idols to moles and bats, then goes into rock clefts and rugged heights as the earth is shaken.

explicit_facts.text: They go into holes of rocks and caves of the earth because the fear of the Lord and the glory of his majesty smite them when he arises to shake the earth.
A man casts his silver and gold idols, made for worship, to the moles and bats.
They go into clefts and tops of ragged rocks because the fear of the Lord and the majesty of his glory smite them when he arises to shake the earth.

reasonable_visual_inferences: A person discarding idols near rock clefts or rugged rocks; moles and bats may be shown as named.
unspecified_visual_details: The people’s identities and appearances, the precise cave or rocks, and how the shaking is shown.
doctrinal_or_story_notes: The passage describes a prophetic day; it does not specify the people or a location.
prohibited_inventions: Showing the Lord visibly; adding injuries, destruction, or details of the shaking not stated.

title: Cease from man
summary: The hearer is told to cease from relying on mortal man, whose breath is in his nostrils, and asked what he is worth.

explicit_facts.text: The verse says to cease from man, whose breath is in his nostrils, and asks wherein he is to be accounted of.

spoken_dialogue.text: Cease ye from man, whose breath is in his nostrils;
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Unspecified speaker

doctrinal_or_story_notes: A concluding exhortation; the verse does not narrate a separate action.
prohibited_inventions: Inventing a visible speaker or specific hearer.
